name: text-roll-navigation

frames.best_why: All six labels are crisp and evenly stacked, with no letter mid-roll obscuring them.

tagline: Six stacked all-caps links roll their letters upward on hover.
summary: A vertical menu of oversized uppercase words stacked tightly. Hovering a word splits it into letters that roll up and away while a fresh copy rises into place, starting from the centre out.
appearance: Six huge white uppercase words in a narrow centred column on black, tightly leaded so the lines almost touch. There are no borders, icons or dividers, only the words.
behaviour: Hovering a word sends each letter upward out of view while a duplicate rises from below with a small stagger from the middle outward. Leaving lets the word settle back.
demo_content: Six links: Home, Components, Pricing, How to use, Account, Login.
use_when: A portfolio or studio site wants a bold text-first menu where the hover motion is the personality.
avoid_when: Six links are hardcoded, the tall stack eats most of a viewport, and it assumes a mouse to reveal the effect.
customise: The six labels and links are hardcoded in the source; the exported TextRoll takes children and a centre flag but styling lives in classes.
weight_why: Six words with per-letter transforms on hover; idle when not hovered.

a11y.note: Items are plain list text with no link or button roles, no focus states and no reduced-motion check.

issues: Words in a label have no space so "How to use" reads as one run-on word.
polish_why: Bold type and a neat letter roll; the lines are cramped and the words run together.
